newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark ends off in U.S. as long positions pared.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark ends off in U.S. as long positions pared.

text.p: The dollar succumbed to profit-taking in thin trade and closed unchanged to lower despite early gains on surprisingly robust U.S. manufacturing data which fueled expectations for higher future U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
The dollar hit session highs against the mark and yen shortly after the Commerce Department announced U.S. durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February.
Analysts had been expecting a 0.4 percent pullback in February to follow January's strong upwardly revised 4.1 percent increase.

"They were pretty good numbers and pointed to more U.S. rate rises. It is my personal opinion that we can see another 50 basis points this year," said Hans Boman, chief spot dealer at Swedbank in New York.
However, the dollar's gains slowly ebbed away in afternoon trade. The greenback closed slightly lower at 1.6873/78 marks from 1.6910/20 at the open and well below its 1.6955 session high.
Against the yen, the dollar also closed below its 124.47 session high at 124.08/13 and just below its opening level of 124.10/20.
On Tuesday, Federal Reserve policymakers raised the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent -- its first rise in more than two years.

The growing prospect for more official U.S. rate hikes in the near-future bolstered the dollar as the gap between U.S. interest rates and those in Japan and Germany could become even more pronounced, dealers said.

Also aiding the dollar was a rise in the pound and active buying of lira for marks on optimism that Italy's leaders will soon issue a mini-budget tailored toward meeting the criteria for joining the proposed European monetary union.
A sneak preview of Italy's 1997 mini-budget was made available on Wednesday but the official, full unveiling should take place on Thursday.

Sterling was boosted by news Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world had narrowed more than expected in January. The data aided sterling as it suggested recent fears that the pound's strength had hurt exporters were premature.
The Office of National Statistics said the global trade deficit narrowed to 641 million pounds ($1 billion), down from 825 million pounds the previous month.
Also, the expectation of sizeable capital outflows from Japan into U.S. assets at the start of the new Japanese financial year next week lent support to the U.S. currency, dealers said.
"We hear there is good interest to buy various U.S. securities from Japanese investors and Japanese trust banks," said Tom Arnold, chief dealer at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.
"It usually happens every April, right after the repatriation period is over and Japan moves into its new (financial) year," he added.

Market players said trading was thin on Wednesday and business was expected to be relatively slow for the remainder of the week as financial markets begin closing early in advance of the Easter weekend. Many bourses will shut down early on Thursday and trading in the United States and much of Europe will remain closed on Friday.

In other trading, the dollar inched lower to 1.4620/30 Swiss francs from 1.4662/72 at the open, but rose to Canadian $1.3734/39 from C$1.3724/29. Sterling rose to $1.6300/10 from $1.6225/35. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7848/53 from $0.7822/27. ((-- Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677))
